claims.claim: Euclid's first major data release covers an area of sky equivalent to 9500 full moons and contains roughly 2.5 trillion pixels.
claims.episode_span: The Wide and Deep Surveys cover an area of sky equivalent to 9500 full moons.
claims.source_title: Euclid lays the foundation for its best-ever 3D map of the universe
claims.supporting_quote: Its first major data set, released now, already contains an astonishing amount of information: images covering an area of sky almost 10,000 times the size of the full moon, around 900 million galaxies and 60 million quasars. In total, the data set contains approximately 2.5 trillion pixels and takes up 1.7 million gigabytes of data.

claims.claim: Some galaxies in Euclid's data release existed when the universe was only 700 million years old.
claims.episode_span: Some galaxies in the data existed when the universe was only 700 million years old.
claims.source_title: Space telescope Euclid sets the new standard for cosmology
claims.supporting_quote: These observations allow astronomers like Kuijken to look far back in time. Some of the galaxies in the data set existed when the universe was only 700 million years old—just 5% of its current age.
